newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX index slips as Wall St opens lower.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX index slips as Wall St opens lower.

text.p: Germany's share market ended more than one percent lower on Thursday, despite earlier notching up fresh record gains, as the Dow Jones index on Wall Street moved lower and market players took profits.
The IBIS DAX ended down 53.15 points at 4,405.52 points, with support at 4,400 holding, but well off records of 4,477.70 points hit earlier in the day.
The blue-chip DAX index had ended on a record closing high of 4,438.93 points earlier on, a rise of 17.21 points.
The German share market has been drawing strength for weeks from the U.S. advance to record levels, so it was not surprising that the market fell as the Dow Jones Industrial lost ground early on.
Some profit-taking was also unsurprising after the heady heights the market has been reaching in recent weeks.
Nonetheless, dealers have set their sights on the 30-share DAX index reaching 4,500 points in the coming days, even though volumes have been lower than in previous days.
The dollar resumed its upward trend against the mark, heading towards 1.84 marks, which helped underpin sentiment.
Daimler-Benz AG stole the spotlight earlier on, ending bourse down 4.50 marks at 154.80 marks despite first-half sales and operating profit figures generally at market expectations.
Daimler shares had risen nearly 10 percent this week ahead of the results, which were released at a news conference in London, and traders tied the losses to profit-taking.
The Stuttgart-based industrial group said operating profit for the first half rose to 1.849 billion marks from 827 million marks in the year-ago period.
Daimler fell back sharply in late trade and ended electronic trade down 4.47 percent at 152.85 marks.
Traders also focused on the banking sector, which has been moving higher on takeover speculation after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank said on July 21 they planned to merge.
Vereinsbank ended the bourse down two marks at 101 marks and Hypo-Bank fell 1.07 marks to 76.53 marks. Insurer Allianz AG, a Hypo-Bank shareholder, fell 9.50 marks to 1,470.
Vereinsbank on Thursday detailed terms of its planned merger with Hypo-Bank, saying its offer to exchange one share in Allianz for six shares in Hypo-Bank would run from August 4 to September 10.
Vereinsbank ended electronic trade down 2.45 marks at 100.30 marks, while Hypo-Bank ended down 1.40 marks at 75.90.
Lufthansa AG initially rose after the Bonn government said it would sell off its remaining stake in the airline this fall, which it said was worth five billion marks.
The share fell with the market later and ended down 25 pfennigs at 36.70 marks.
